comment: Memory retained per request, in MB, for the routes most able to hurt production. Measured by scripts/memory-check.sh against the local prod-restore. Run-to-run spread on an identical build is ~3%, so toleranceRatio sits far outside the noise while still catching real regressions: the /shows/year filter path went 9.60 -> 16.10 (+68%) between two shipped PRs, which this would have failed. Baselines are both machine-relative and specific to requestsPerRoute, since fixed warmup cost amortizes over however many requests the run makes — always re-baseline with `make mem-check-update` rather than editing these numbers by hand, and treat a baseline change in a diff as something to justify.

routes.name: year-listing
routes.why: Highest-traffic route and the one production crawlers walk hardest.

routes.name: year-listing-filtered
routes.why: Filter permutations are ~100% of the year traffic production actually sees, and they cost more than the bare URL since the loader returns the whole year regardless.

routes.name: shows-stats
routes.why: Ships the entire catalog on every request; the most expensive single payload in the app.
